subject: Humanities
objective_verbatim: Recognise people who stood up for fairness (Int'l Women's Day).
unit_verbatim: Caring & fairness, stories that teach us
source_authority: Current owner brief supplies exact outcome, date, period and five-week calendar. Archived scheme corroborates outcome and term context; owner calendar overrides its six-week label.

BUILD Weekly - Spring.C49: Recognise people who stood up for fairness (Int'l Women's Day).

BUILD - Spring.D11: Caring & fairness, stories that teach us
BUILD - Spring.E11: Recognise right/kind actions in stories; talk about fairness; identify ways to care for others.

scaffold_level.label: Level 2 scaffolds
scaffold_level.meaning: word bank, sentence starter and visible model on every task and route

minimum_finish: Recognise both named historical people, link each to an action and fairness aim, and give one linked line about either through the usual response mode, with actual help recorded.

historical_people.name: Rosa Parks
historical_people.label: A
historical_people.action: She kept her bus seat in 1955.
historical_people.facts: She said no to an unfair bus rule. The rule treated Black people unfairly.
historical_people.fairness: Black people should be treated fairly.

historical_people.name: Millicent Fawcett
historical_people.label: B
historical_people.action: She led a peaceful group for women’s votes.
historical_people.facts: She gave talks and worked with others. They asked for women to vote.
historical_people.fairness: Women should have a fair say in who makes the rules.

portrait_status: Newly made teaching drawings; not archival photographs
observance: International Women’s Day was on 8 March this month; lesson date 18 March.

evidence.description: Both historical recognition/action/aim links, one-line response, actual reading mode and support

feedback_gate: Voice and audience reply present; one NS and pupil own response before R; actual banking before E.
careers_line: Listen, seek fair treatment through safe agreed routes and work with others.
communication_portfolio: Offer the authentic explanation to the Communication portfolio.

slides.title: People and fairness
slides.text:
Meet two people from the past.
Match each name and action.
Give one line about one person.
You can point or ask an adult to write.

slides.title: Ready to start
slides.text:
Choose: ready, rest or help.
You can point in a quiet way.
Start: I feel __.
Model: I feel ready.
You can pause with an adult.

slides.title: Names and clues
slides.text:
Look at the two labelled drawings.
Match each name with a cue: bus seat or vote.
An adult can read both names.
Words: seat, vote, match. Start: I match __ with __.
Model: I match Rosa Parks with the bus seat.

slides.title: Our people task
slides.text:
Recognise people who stood up for fairness (Int'l Women's Day).
Show both people. Match names, actions and fair aims.
In your book: give one line about one person.
Words: fair, rule, seat, vote, group, help.
Start: __ stood up for fairness.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: Two people from the past
slides.text:
New drawings. Left: Rosa Parks. Right: Millicent Fawcett.
Many people worked for change. The day was on 8 March this month.
Words: seat, vote, fair. Start: __ stood up for __.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: Match the links
slides.text:
Rosa Parks: kept her bus seat in 1955.
Fair aim: Black people should be treated fairly.
Millicent Fawcett: led a peaceful group for women’s votes.
Fair aim: women should have a fair say.
They worked with lots of people.
Words: fair, rule, seat, vote, group, help.
Start: __ stood up for fairness.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: Show the person
slides.text:
Who worked with a group for women’s votes?
Use the two labels. An adult can read them.
Show the person and the action in a quiet way.
Words: fair, rule, seat, vote, group, help.
Start: __ stood up for fairness.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: My book line
slides.text:
Supported: point to both people and use cues.
Independent: match both people, actions and aims.
Aspire: match both and say how one action was fair.
In your book: give one line about one person.
Words: fair, rule, seat, vote, group, help.
Start: __ stood up for fairness.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: My quiet check
slides.text:
Show both people and their actions.
Read or listen to your one line.
Keep or change it after one next step.
Words: fair, rule, seat, vote, group, help.
Start: __ stood up for fairness.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: My last step
slides.text:
Show each person when an adult reads the name.
Show one action for each.
Share your book line in a quiet way.
Words: fair, rule, seat, vote, group, help.
Start: __ stood up for fairness.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: Words that help
slides.text:
fair: people are treated with the same worth.
rule: a set way people are told to act.
seat: a place to sit. vote: a choice about who makes rules.
group: people who work together.
stood up for: spoke or acted for fair rules.
Start: __ stood up for fairness.
Model: Rosa Parks stood up for fair bus rules.

slides.title: Adult support brief
slides.text:
Three to four pupils. Use Pupil number: ____ for each pupil.
10, 15 and 15 minute blocks; brief resets within.
Keep word bank, starter and model on EVERY task.
Read names; check recognition through pointing or matching.
No public questions, cold calling or required reading aloud.
No personal disclosure or discrimination reenactment.
R: Voice + audience reply + one NS + own response.
E: actual banking. Record reading mode and actual help.
